import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function using entropy-modulated Best Fit heuristic for bin selection.
    
    Implementation: Combines Best Fit logic with entropy-based fragmentation
    assessment. Uses Shannon entropy to measure bin distribution uniformity
    and adaptively adjusts penalties and thresholds accordingly.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Calculate entropy of the bin distribution for fragmentation assessment
    # Normalize capacities to form a probability distribution
    total_capacity = np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
    if total_capacity > 0:
        p = bins_remain_cap / total_capacity
        # Filter out zero probabilities to avoid log(0)
        p = p[p > 0]
        
        # Shannon entropy calculation
        entropy = -np.sum(p * np.log(p + 1e-10))  # Add small epsilon to prevent log(0)
        
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible value for this distribution size
        n_bins = len(bins_remain_cap)
        if n_bins > 1:
            max_entropy = np.log(n_bins)  # Maximum entropy for uniform distribution
            if max_entropy > 0:
                normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy
            else:
                normalized_entropy = 0.0
        else:
            normalized_entropy = 0.0
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Calculate quantiles as dynamic reference points
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        q25, q50, q75 = np.percentile(bins_remain_cap, [25, 50, 75])
        # Use interquartile range as a measure of capacity spread
        iqr = q75 - q25
    else:
        q25 = q50 = q75 = bins_remain_cap[0]
        iqr = 0.0
    
    # Adaptive gap threshold based on quantiles and entropy
    base_gap_threshold = max(q25 * 0.3, item * 0.4)  # At least 30% of 25th percentile or 40% of item
    adaptive_gap_threshold = base_gap_threshold + 0.1 * iqr  # Add IQR component to adapt to spread
    
    # Adjust threshold based on entropy - higher entropy suggests more uniform distribution
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    adjusted_gap_threshold = adaptive_gap_threshold * entropy_factor
    
    # Penalty for bins that would create small gaps (fragmentation)
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < adjusted_gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * 7.0,  # Fixed penalty multiplier based on parent success
        0.0
    )
    
    # Bonus for bins that would leave capacity near the median (promotes reuse of common sizes)
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - q50) < max(0.1 * q50, item * 0.1),
        item * 0.22,  # Same as parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Adaptive efficiency bonus based on entropy
    # When entropy is low (bins are more similar), being efficient is more important
    efficiency_base_bonus = item * 0.18
    efficiency_entropy_scale = 1.0 - 0.3 * normalized_entropy  # Less bonus when entropy is high
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < max(0.1 * q25, item * 0.1),  # Use 10% of 25th percentile as reference
        efficiency_base_bonus * efficiency_entropy_scale,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins with moderate leftover capacity
    cap_mean = bins_remain_cap.mean() if len(bins_remain_cap) > 0 else bins_remain_cap[0] if len(bins_remain_cap) == 1 else 0.0
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > max(0.05 * cap_mean, item * 0.05)) & 
        (remaining_after_placement < max(0.3 * cap_mean, item * 0.3)),
        item * 0.08,  # Same as parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus
    
    return scores

        remaining_after_placement * 7.0,  # Fixed penalty multiplier based on parent success
        0.0
    )
    
    # Bonus for bins that would leave capacity near the median (promotes reuse of common sizes)
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - q50) < max(0.1 * q50, item * 0.1),
        item * 0.22,  # Same as parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Adaptive efficiency bonus based on entropy
    # When entropy is low (bins are more similar), being efficient is more important
    efficiency_base_bonus = item * 0.18
    efficiency_entropy_scale = 1.0 - 0.3 * normalized_entropy  # Less bonus when entropy is high
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < max(0.1 * q25, item * 0.1),  # Use 10% of 25th percentile as reference
        efficiency_base_bonus * efficiency_entropy_scale,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins with moderate leftover capacity
    cap_mean = bins_remain_cap.mean() if len(bins_remain_cap) > 0 else bins_remain_cap[0] if len(bins_remain_cap) == 1 else 0.0
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > max(0.05 * cap_mean, item * 0.05)) & 
        (remaining_after_placement < max(0.3 * cap_mean, item * 0.3)),
        item * 0.08,  # Same as parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function using entropy-modulated Best Fit heuristic for bin selection.
    
    Implementation: Combines Best Fit logic with entropy-based fragmentation
    assessment. Uses Shannon entropy to measure bin distribution uniformity
    and adaptively adjusts penalties and thresholds accordingly.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Calculate entropy of the bin distribution for fragmentation assessment
    # Normalize capacities to form a probability distribution
    total_capacity = np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
    if total_capacity > 0:
        p = bins_remain_cap / total_capacity
        # Filter out zero probabilities to avoid log(0)
        p = p[p > 0]
        
        # Shannon entropy calculation
        entropy = -np.sum(p * np.log(p + 1e-10))  # Add small epsilon to prevent log(0)
        
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible value for this distribution size
        n_bins = len(bins_remain_cap)
        if n_bins > 1:
            max_entropy = np.log(n_bins)  # Maximum entropy for uniform distribution
            if max_entropy > 0:
                normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy
            else:
                normalized_entropy = 0.0
        else:
            normalized_entropy = 0.0
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use fixed parameters based on parent solution success
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0)  # Fixed threshold from parent solution
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy  # Entropy modulation
    adjusted_gap_threshold = gap_threshold * entropy_factor
    
    # Penalty for bins that would create small gaps (fragmentation)
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < adjusted_gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * 7.0,  # Fixed penalty multiplier from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Simple combination of components
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with entropy-modulated Best Fit heuristic and inferred temporal context.
    
    Implementation: Combines entropy-modulated Best Fit with a lightweight, stateless proxy
    for temporal context derived from the current distribution of bin residuals. The method
    analyzes the shape of the residual capacity histogram (via skewness, mode location, and
    ratio of small residuals) to infer whether the system is in a 'small-item' or 'large-item'
    regime. This inferred regime is used to dynamically adjust gap thresholds and matching
    bonuses in real time, enabling context-aware adaptation without violating online or
    stateless constraints. This bridges the performance gap between purely reactive and
    trend-aware heuristics.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Calculate entropy of the remaining capacity distribution
    # Normalize capacities to probabilities
    total_capacity = bins_remain_cap.sum()
    if total_capacity > 0:
        probs = bins_remain_cap / total_capacity
        # Avoid log(0) by masking zero probabilities
        probs = probs[probs > 0]
        if len(probs) > 0:
            entropy = -np.sum(probs * np.log2(probs))
            # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy for this number of bins
            max_entropy = np.log2(len(bins_remain_cap)) if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1 else 1.0
            normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy if max_entropy > 0 else 0.0
        else:
            normalized_entropy = 0.0
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Infer the current regime based on the distribution of bin residuals
    # Calculate regime indicators
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 0:
        max_cap = bins_remain_cap.max()
        if max_cap > 0:
            # Ratio of small residuals (indicating fragmented state)
            small_residual_ratio = np.sum(remaining_after_placement < 0.1 * max_cap) / len(remaining_after_placement)
            
            # Skewness of the remaining capacity distribution
            mean_cap = bins_remain_cap.mean()
            std_cap = bins_remain_cap.std()
            if std_cap > 0:
                skewness = np.mean(((bins_remain_cap - mean_cap) / std_cap) ** 3)
            else:
                skewness = 0.0
                
            # Mode-like indicator (most common range of remaining capacity)
            if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
                hist, bin_edges = np.histogram(bins_remain_cap, bins=min(10, len(bins_remain_cap)))
                mode_idx = np.argmax(hist)
                mode_range_center = (bin_edges[mode_idx] + bin_edges[mode_idx + 1]) / 2
            else:
                mode_range_center = bins_remain_cap[0]
        else:
            small_residual_ratio = 0.0
            skewness = 0.0
            mode_range_center = 0.0
    else:
        small_residual_ratio = 0.0
        skewness = 0.0
        mode_range_center = 0.0
    
    # Dynamic adjustment factor based on regime inference
    # Adjust based on how fragmented the system appears
    fragmentation_indicator = small_residual_ratio
    regime_factor = 1.0 + 0.5 * fragmentation_indicator - 0.3 * abs(skewness)
    
    # Entropy-modulated factor enhanced with regime awareness
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 1.2 * normalized_entropy * regime_factor
    
    # Calculate quantiles as dynamic reference points
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        q25, q50, q75 = np.percentile(bins_remain_cap, [25, 50, 75])
    else:
        q25 = q50 = q75 = bins_remain_cap[0]
    
    # Gap threshold based on entropy and regime modulation
    base_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.35, 5.0)  # Slightly reduced from 0.40 and 6.0 for tighter packing
    adaptive_gap_threshold = base_gap_threshold * entropy_factor
    
    # Penalty for bins that would create small gaps (fragmentation)
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < adaptive_gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * 8.0,  # Increased from 7.0 for stronger fragmentation penalty
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave capacity close to the median
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - q50) < 0.08 * q50,  # Reduced tolerance from 0.1 to 0.08
        item * 0.25 * regime_factor,  # Increased from 0.22 for stronger median matching preference, modulated by regime
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < 0.08 * bins_remain_cap.max(),  # Reduced from 0.1 to 0.08 for stricter efficiency
        item * 0.20 * regime_factor,  # Increased from 0.18 for stronger efficiency preference, modulated by regime
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins with moderate leftover capacity
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > 0.04 * bins_remain_cap.mean()) & 
        (remaining_after_placement < 0.25 * bins_remain_cap.mean()),  # Reduced from 0.05 and 0.3 to 0.04 and 0.25
        item * 0.10 * regime_factor,  # Increased from 0.08 for stronger consolidation preference, modulated by regime
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional entropy-based bonus for bins that contribute to reducing entropy (better consolidation)
    # Calculate what the entropy would be if we placed the item in each bin
    temp_remaining = remaining_after_placement
    
    # Filter out bins with zero or negative capacity for entropy calculation
    positive_caps = temp_remaining[temp_remaining > 0]
    
    if len(positive_caps) > 1 and positive_caps.sum() > 0:
        temp_probs = positive_caps / positive_caps.sum()
        temp_probs = temp_probs[temp_probs > 0]
        if len(temp_probs) > 0:
            temp_entropy = -np.sum(temp_probs * np.log2(temp_probs))
            max_temp_entropy = np.log2(len(positive_caps)) if len(positive_caps) > 1 else 1.0
            normalized_temp_entropy = temp_entropy / max_temp_entropy if max_temp_entropy > 0 else 0.0
            # Prefer moves that lead to lower entropy (better consolidation)
            entropy_reduction_bonus = (normalized_entropy - normalized_temp_entropy) * item * 7.0  # Increased from 5.0
        else:
            entropy_reduction_bonus = 0.0
    else:
        entropy_reduction_bonus = 0.0
    
    # Capacity distribution bonus - rewards moves that lead to more uniform capacity distribution
    # This encourages consolidation toward similar remaining capacities
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        positive_remaining = remaining_after_placement[remaining_after_placement > 0]
        if len(positive_remaining) > 1:
            capacity_std = np.std(positive_remaining)
            capacity_mean = np.mean(positive_remaining)
            if capacity_mean > 0:
                cv = capacity_std / capacity_mean  # Coefficient of variation
                # Lower CV means more uniform distribution, so reward moves that decrease CV
                uniformity_bonus = (1.0 - cv) * item * 0.15  # Reward for uniformity
            else:
                uniformity_bonus = 0.0
        else:
            uniformity_bonus = 0.0
    else:
        uniformity_bonus = 0.0
    
    # Regime-dependent consolidation bonus based on inferred context
    # If the system appears to be in a fragmented state, emphasize consolidation
    if fragmentation_indicator > 0.5:  # High fragmentation detected
        fragmentation_consolidation_bonus = item * 0.30
    else:
        fragmentation_consolidation_bonus = 0.0
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (
        best_fit_score 
        - gap_penalty 
        + matching_bonus 
        + efficiency_bonus 
        + consolidation_bonus 
        + entropy_reduction_bonus 
        + uniformity_bonus
        + fragmentation_consolidation_bonus
    )

    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with entropy-modulated Best Fit heuristic.
    
    Implementation: Uses entropy-modulated Best Fit approach with quantile-based
    gap thresholds and strategic bonuses for optimal bin selection. This provides
    a balance between tight packing and fragmentation avoidance.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Calculate entropy of the remaining capacity distribution
    # Normalize capacities to probabilities
    total_capacity = bins_remain_cap.sum()
    if total_capacity > 0:
        probs = bins_remain_cap / total_capacity
        # Avoid log(0) by masking zero probabilities
        probs = probs[probs > 0]
        if len(probs) > 0:
            entropy = -np.sum(probs * np.log2(probs))
            # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy for this number of bins
            max_entropy = np.log2(len(bins_remain_cap)) if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1 else 1.0
            normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy if max_entropy > 0 else 0.0
        else:
            normalized_entropy = 0.0
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Entropy-modulated factor
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 1.2 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Calculate quantiles as dynamic reference points
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        q25, q50, q75 = np.percentile(bins_remain_cap, [25, 50, 75])
    else:
        q25 = q50 = q75 = bins_remain_cap[0]
    
    # Gap threshold based on entropy modulation
    base_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.35, 5.0)
    adaptive_gap_threshold = base_gap_threshold * entropy_factor
    
    # Penalty for bins that would create small gaps (fragmentation)
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < adaptive_gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * 8.0,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave capacity close to the median
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - q50) < 0.08 * q50,
        item * 0.25,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < 0.08 * bins_remain_cap.max(),
        item * 0.20,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins with moderate leftover capacity
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > 0.04 * bins_remain_cap.mean()) & 
        (remaining_after_placement < 0.25 * bins_remain_cap.mean()),
        item * 0.10,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional entropy-based bonus for bins that contribute to reducing entropy (better consolidation)
    # Calculate what the entropy would be if we placed the item in each bin
    temp_remaining = remaining_after_placement
    
    # Filter out bins with zero or negative capacity for entropy calculation
    positive_caps = temp_remaining[temp_remaining > 0]
    
    if len(positive_caps) > 1 and positive_caps.sum() > 0:
        temp_probs = positive_caps / positive_caps.sum()
        temp_probs = temp_probs[temp_probs > 0]
        if len(temp_probs) > 0:
            temp_entropy = -np.sum(temp_probs * np.log2(temp_probs))
            max_temp_entropy = np.log2(len(positive_caps)) if len(positive_caps) > 1 else 1.0
            normalized_temp_entropy = temp_entropy / max_temp_entropy if max_temp_entropy > 0 else 0.0
            # Prefer moves that lead to lower entropy (better consolidation)
            entropy_reduction_bonus = (normalized_entropy - normalized_temp_entropy) * item * 7.0
        else:
            entropy_reduction_bonus = 0.0
    else:
        entropy_reduction_bonus = 0.0
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (
        best_fit_score 
        - gap_penalty 
        + matching_bonus 
        + efficiency_bonus 
        + consolidation_bonus 
        + entropy_reduction_bonus 
    )

    return scores

import numpy as np
import threading

# Global variables for thread-safe instance tracking
_instance_state = threading.local()

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with temporal-awareness through instance-local item trend tracking.
    
    Implementation: Maintains a circular buffer of the last N items to track size trends
    within the current instance. Uses this temporal context to dynamically reweight
    priority components: in small-item-dominant regimes, increases matching and 
    consolidation bonuses to encourage reuse of fragmented space; in large-item-dominant
    regimes, suppresses gap penalties and emphasizes pure Best Fit behavior.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    global _instance_state
    
    # Initialize instance-specific tracker if not present
    if not hasattr(_instance_state, 'item_buffer'):
        _instance_state.item_buffer = []  # Circular buffer to store recent items
        _instance_state.buffer_size = 15  # Size of the sliding window
    
    # Add current item to the circular buffer
    _instance_state.item_buffer.append(item)
    if len(_instance_state.item_buffer) > _instance_state.buffer_size:
        _instance_state.item_buffer.pop(0)  # Remove oldest item if buffer exceeds size
    
    # Analyze the current size regime based on the recent items
    if len(_instance_state.item_buffer) > 0:
        recent_items = np.array(_instance_state.item_buffer)
        mean_size = np.mean(recent_items)
        std_size = np.std(recent_items) if len(recent_items) > 1 else 0
        
        # Classify the regime based on the current item vs recent mean
        if mean_size > 0:
            size_regime_factor = item / mean_size
        else:
            size_regime_factor = 1.0
    else:
        size_regime_factor = 1.0
    
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        # Reset the buffer when no bins are valid (end of instance)
        _instance_state.item_buffer = []
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Adjust parameters based on the size regime
    # For small items relative to recent trend, emphasize space reuse
    if size_regime_factor <= 0.7:  # Small item regime
        regime_multiplier = 1.2  # Increase bonuses
        regime_penalty_multiplier = 0.8  # Reduce penalties
    elif size_regime_factor >= 1.5:  # Large item regime
        regime_multiplier = 0.8  # Reduce bonuses
        regime_penalty_multiplier = 1.2  # Increase penalties to avoid fragmentation
    else:  # Normal regime
        regime_multiplier = 1.0
        regime_penalty_multiplier = 1.0
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy and regime factors
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor * regime_penalty_multiplier
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor * regime_penalty_multiplier
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave a good residual capacity
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - item * 0.2) < item * 0.05,
        item * 0.22 * regime_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional bonus for bins that would be filled very efficiently
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < item * 0.1,
        item * 0.18 * regime_multiplier,
        0.0
    )

    # Bonus for bins that are moderately filled to encourage consolidation
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > item * 0.1) & (remaining_after_placement < item * 0.3),
        item * 0.08 * regime_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Weight for best fit based on regime
    best_fit_weight = 1.0
    
    # Combine all components with dynamic weights
    scores = (best_fit_weight * best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus)
    
    return scores

        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave a good residual capacity
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - item * 0.2) < item * 0.05,
        item * 0.22,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional bonus for bins that would be filled very efficiently
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < item * 0.1,
        item * 0.18,
        0.0
    )

    # Bonus for bins that are moderately filled to encourage consolidation
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > item * 0.1) & (remaining_after_placement < item * 0.3),
        item * 0.08,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus)
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with item trend tracking and entropy-based dynamic parameter adjustment.
    
    Implementation: Combines Best Fit logic with dynamic gap penalties and bonuses,
    where parameters are adjusted based on both entropy of bin capacities (fragmentation awareness)
    and real-time size regime indicators from a circular buffer of recent items.
    The trend tracker computes regime indicators (fraction of small, medium, large items)
    to dynamically scale scoring component weights, while maintaining online compliance
    through instance-local state that resets at each new problem.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Global state variables - these will be reset at the start of each new instance
    if not hasattr(priority, 'item_buffer'):
        priority.item_buffer = []  # Circular buffer to track recent items
        priority.buffer_size = 15  # Size of the sliding window
    
    # For this implementation, we'll simulate instance-level reset behavior by checking if this is a new instance
    # In practice, the entire function state should be reset per instance
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1000:  # Heuristic to detect new instance (based on starting with many empty bins)
        priority.item_buffer = []  # Reset buffer at beginning of new instance

    # Add current item to the buffer
    priority.item_buffer.append(item)
    if len(priority.item_buffer) > priority.buffer_size:
        priority.item_buffer.pop(0)  # Remove oldest item to maintain buffer size
    
    # Calculate trend-based weights based on recent item distribution
    if len(priority.item_buffer) > 0:
        recent_items = np.array(priority.item_buffer)
        # Define size regimes: small (< 0.3*capacity), medium (0.3-0.7*capacity), large (> 0.7*capacity)
        # Using median of recent items to normalize
        if len(recent_items) > 0:
            median_size = np.median(recent_items)
            if median_size > 0:
                small_items = np.sum(recent_items < 0.3 * median_size) / len(recent_items)
                large_items = np.sum(recent_items > 0.7 * median_size) / len(recent_items)
            else:
                small_items = 0.0
                large_items = 0.0
        else:
            small_items = 0.0
            large_items = 0.0
    else:
        small_items = 0.0
        large_items = 0.0

    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Adjust parameters based on both entropy and trend indicators
    # Increase matching bonus during small-item dominance
    matching_bonus_weight = 0.22 * (1.0 + 0.5 * small_items)
    # Increase efficiency bonus during large-item dominance
    efficiency_bonus_weight = 0.18 * (1.0 + 0.5 * large_items)
    # Increase gap penalty when fragmentation is high
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave a good residual capacity
    # This helps with packing efficiency by creating useful remaining spaces
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - item * 0.2) < item * 0.05,
        item * matching_bonus_weight,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional bonus for bins that would be filled very efficiently
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < item * 0.1,
        item * efficiency_bonus_weight,
        0.0
    )

    # Add a bonus for bins that are moderately filled to encourage consolidation
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > item * 0.1) & (remaining_after_placement < item * 0.3),
        item * 0.08,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with entropy-based dynamic parameter adjustment.
    
    Implementation: Combines Best Fit logic with dynamic gap penalties and bonuses,
    where parameters are adjusted based on entropy of bin capacities (fragmentation awareness).
    This follows the successful approach from the parent solution that achieved 2028.4 bins.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Use parameters from the successful parent solution
    # Increase matching bonus during small-item dominance
    matching_bonus_weight = 0.22
    # Increase efficiency bonus during large-item dominance  
    efficiency_bonus_weight = 0.18
    # Increase gap penalty when fragmentation is high
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave a good residual capacity
    # This helps with packing efficiency by creating useful remaining spaces
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - item * 0.2) < item * 0.05,
        item * matching_bonus_weight,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional bonus for bins that would be filled very efficiently
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < item * 0.1,
        item * efficiency_bonus_weight,
        0.0
    )

    # Add a bonus for bins that are moderately filled to encourage consolidation
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement > item * 0.1) & (remaining_after_placement < item * 0.3),
        item * 0.08,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with adaptive residual targets based on bin state distribution.
    
    Implementation: Replace fixed percentage-based bonus thresholds with adaptive 
    residual targets derived from the current bin state distribution. Compute the 
    mode or median of existing bin remainders and align matching/consolidation 
    bonuses to residuals near this value, enabling the heuristic to dynamically 
    adapt to the emergent fragmentation pattern rather than relying on static 
    item-relative ratios. This builds on successful entropy-based dynamic 
    parameter adjustment from parent solutions while addressing the limitation 
    of fixed percentages failing to generalize across diverse item size distributions.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Adaptive residual targets based on current bin state distribution
    # Use median of current remaining capacities as reference point
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 0:
        # Calculate adaptive targets based on current bin state
        current_median = np.median(bins_remain_cap)
        current_mean = np.mean(bins_remain_cap)
        
        # Use the minimum of median and mean to focus on smaller, more common residuals
        adaptive_target = min(current_median, current_mean)
        
        # Ensure target is not too small to be meaningful
        adaptive_target = max(adaptive_target, item * 0.1, 1.0)
    else:
        # Fallback to item-relative target if no bins
        adaptive_target = item * 0.2
    
    # Matching bonus for bins that would leave a residual near the adaptive target
    matching_tolerance = max(adaptive_target * 0.25, item * 0.05)  # Adaptive tolerance
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - adaptive_target) < matching_tolerance,
        adaptive_target * 0.5,  # Scale bonus with the adaptive target
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled
    efficiency_threshold = max(item * 0.1, 2.0)  # Minimum absolute threshold
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < efficiency_threshold,
        item * 0.18,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Adaptive consolidation bonus based on current bin state
    # Define consolidation range around the adaptive target
    consolidation_lower = max(adaptive_target * 0.5, item * 0.05)
    consolidation_upper = min(adaptive_target * 1.5, item * 0.5)
    
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= consolidation_lower) & 
        (remaining_after_placement <= consolidation_upper),
        adaptive_target * 0.25,  # Scale bonus with the adaptive target
        0.0
    )
    
    # Additional bonus for bins that are already quite full to encourage closure
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 0:
        # Find bins that are already more than half full
        high_utilization_threshold = np.mean(bins_remain_cap) * 0.7
        high_utilization_bonus = np.where(
            bins_remain_cap < (100 - high_utilization_threshold),  # Assuming capacity 100, adjust accordingly
            np.where(remaining_after_placement <= high_utilization_threshold,
                     item * 0.1,
                     0.0),
            0.0
        )
    else:
        high_utilization_bonus = np.zeros_like(remaining_after_placement)
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus +
              high_utilization_bonus)
    
    return scores
=======
import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with simplified adaptive elements and proven parameters from parent solutions.
    
    Implementation: Return to the proven entropy-based dynamic parameter adjustment from 
    parent solutions while maintaining some adaptive elements. The original adaptive target 
    system appears to have caused performance degradation compared to the parent solution.
    Focus on stable, well-calibrated bonus structures with entropy-based dynamic adjustment.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Fixed percentage-based matching bonus (from parent solution)
    matching_target = item * 0.2
    matching_tolerance = item * 0.05  # Fixed tolerance based on item size
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - matching_target) < matching_tolerance,
        item * 0.22,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled (from parent solution)
    efficiency_threshold = max(item * 0.1, 2.0)  # Minimum absolute threshold
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < efficiency_threshold,
        item * 0.18,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins that would leave moderate residual space (from parent solution)
    consolidation_lower = item * 0.1
    consolidation_upper = item * 0.3
    
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= consolidation_lower) & 
        (remaining_after_placement <= consolidation_upper),
        item * 0.08,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus)
    
    return scores

>>>[ExperimentAgent] Final summary after 2 experiments:
The experiment series investigated an evolutionary approach to designing a priority heuristic for the Online Bin Packing Problem, aiming to minimize bin usage while adapting to dynamic item size distributions. Key findings reveal that solution performance is highly sensitive to parameter complexity and balance. The initial attempt to implement a quantile-based dynamic adjustment using item-size regimes (small/medium/large) actually degraded performance from 2028.4 to 2033.0 bins (1.60% → 1.83% excess over lower bound), demonstrating that added complexity without proper state tracking harms results. Performance trends show a clear plateau approximately 32 bins above the theoretical optimum (1996.4), suggesting fundamental limitations of purely reactive, state-only policies that lack memory of recent item sequences. Parameter insights indicate that entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy effectively modulates gap penalties based on bin fragmentation, while fixed weights (matching_bonus_weight=0.22, efficiency_bonus_weight=0.18) and thresholds (gap_threshold = max(item*0.40, 6.0)) provide robust performance across item sizes. The documented failure was attempting to simulate quantile tracking using only the current item as a proxy, which violated the core requirement of maintaining instance-local historical context. Successful techniques included entropy-normalized fragmentation awareness combined with carefully balanced bonus/penalty components that encourage both efficient packing and useful residual space creation. Unresolved issues include the inability to adapt to shifting item size distributions without external state management, as the current online-compliant implementation cannot track recent item history. Actionable recommendations for future research include: (1) implementing a proper resettable quantile tracker with decaying histograms that maintains instance-local state through external orchestration, (2) exploring hybrid approaches that combine the proven entropy-based framework with genuine distribution-aware adaptation, and (3) investigating whether breaking the purely reactive paradigm through limited look-ahead or learning mechanisms could overcome the observed 32-bin performance ceiling.

Future work must prioritize lightweight, externally resettable memory mechanisms—such as quantile trackers over recent items—that respect online compliance while enabling genuine distributional adaptation. Hybridizing the proven entropy-aware framework with such minimal predictive features offers the most promising path to breach the current performance plateau. The key lesson is clear: the bottleneck is not heuristic expressivity, but the informational interface between item history and bin-state evaluation.

import numpy as np
import threading

# Thread-local storage for item trend tracking
_thread_local = threading.local()

def _get_item_trend_buffer():
    """Get or initialize the item trend buffer for the current thread."""
    if not hasattr(_thread_local, 'buffer'):
        _thread_local.buffer = np.zeros(10)  # Circular buffer of size 10
        _thread_local.index = 0
        _thread_local.is_full = False
    return _thread_local.buffer, _thread_local.index, _thread_local.is_full

def _update_item_trend(item, bin_capacity=100.0):
    """Update the item trend buffer with the new item and return the moving average."""
    buffer, index, is_full = _get_item_trend_buffer()
    
    # Add new item to circular buffer
    buffer[index] = item
    index = (index + 1) % len(buffer)
    
    # Check if buffer is full now
    if index == 0:
        is_full = True
    
    # Update thread local values
    _thread_local.buffer = buffer
    _thread_local.index = index
    _thread_local.is_full = is_full
    
    # Calculate moving average
    if is_full:
        avg_recent_items = np.mean(buffer)
    else:
        avg_recent_items = np.mean(buffer[:index])
    
    # Return relative size compared to bin capacity
    return avg_recent_items / bin_capacity

def _reset_item_trend():
    """Reset the item trend buffer for a new instance."""
    _thread_local.buffer = np.zeros(10)
    _thread_local.index = 0
    _thread_local.is_full = False

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with entropy-based dynamic penalties and lightweight item trend detection.
    
    Implementation: Hybridize entropy-based dynamic penalties with a lightweight, instance-local 
    item size trend detector that uses a circular buffer (N=10) to compute the moving average 
    of recent item sizes. Use this trend to modulate the weights of the matching and 
    consolidation bonuses—when recent items are consistently small (<0.3 of bin capacity), 
    boost the matching bonus weight by up to 30% to encourage reuse of fragmented space; 
    when items are large (>0.6), suppress all bonuses except efficiency to mimic Best Fit behavior.
    The trend signal is smoothed to prevent noise-induced oscillations. The implementation 
    builds on the successful parent solution with entropy-based dynamic parameter adjustment.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Reset trend detector if this is the first call in a new instance (indicated by a large number of bins)
    # This heuristic assumes that when many bins are available, it's likely the start of an instance
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 50:  # Heuristic: assume new instance starts with many empty bins
        _reset_item_trend()
    
    # Update and retrieve item trend information
    # We'll use a default bin capacity of 100.0 based on the evaluation script info
    avg_item_ratio = _update_item_trend(item, bin_capacity=100.0)
    
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are
        bin_probs = bins_remain_cap / np.sum(bins_remain_cap)
        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Adjust bonus weights based on item trend
    # When items are small, boost matching and consolidation bonuses to reuse fragmented space
    # When items are large, suppress bonuses except efficiency to mimic Best Fit
    if avg_item_ratio < 0.3:  # Small items
        matching_weight_factor = 1.3  # Boost by 30%
        consolidation_weight_factor = 1.2  # Boost by 20%
        efficiency_weight_factor = 1.0
    elif avg_item_ratio > 0.6:  # Large items
        matching_weight_factor = 0.5  # Reduce
        consolidation_weight_factor = 0.5  # Reduce
        efficiency_weight_factor = 1.1  # Slightly increase
    else:  # Medium items
        matching_weight_factor = 1.0
        consolidation_weight_factor = 1.0
        efficiency_weight_factor = 1.0
    
    # Fixed percentage-based matching bonus (from parent solution), adjusted by trend factor
    matching_target = item * 0.2
    matching_tolerance = item * 0.05  # Fixed tolerance based on item size
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - matching_target) < matching_tolerance,
        item * 0.22 * matching_weight_factor,  # Proven value from parent solution, adjusted by trend
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled (from parent solution), adjusted by trend
    efficiency_threshold = max(item * 0.1, 2.0)  # Minimum absolute threshold
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < efficiency_threshold,
        item * 0.18 * efficiency_weight_factor,  # Proven value from parent solution, adjusted by trend
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins that would leave moderate residual space (from parent solution), adjusted by trend
    consolidation_lower = item * 0.1
    consolidation_upper = item * 0.3
    
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= consolidation_lower) & 
        (remaining_after_placement <= consolidation_upper),
        item * 0.08 * consolidation_weight_factor,  # Proven value from parent solution, adjusted by trend
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus)
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with entropy-based dynamic penalties (based on successful parent solution).
    
    Implementation: Use entropy-based dynamic parameter adjustment with fixed percentage-based 
    bonuses as proven effective in parent solutions. This removes the complex trend detector 
    that was causing performance degradation.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """

    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])

    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item

    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity

    if len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        # Bin state entropy: measure how uniform the remaining capacities are

        bin_entropy = -np.sum(bin_probs * np.log(bin_probs + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
        normalized_entropy = bin_entropy / np.log(len(bins_remain_cap))
    else:
        normalized_entropy = 0.0
    
    # Use local statistics to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher entropy suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    entropy_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_entropy
    
    # Set parameters based on entropy factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * entropy_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * entropy_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )

        item * 0.22,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled (from parent solution)
    efficiency_threshold = max(item * 0.1, 2.0)  # Minimum absolute threshold
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < efficiency_threshold,
        item * 0.18,  # Proven value from parent solution

    consolidation_lower = item * 0.1
    consolidation_upper = item * 0.3

        (remaining_after_placement >= consolidation_lower) & 
        (remaining_after_placement <= consolidation_upper),

        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty +

    return scores

Persistent challenges include the ~32-bin gap from the theoretical optimum (1996.4), suggesting fundamental limitations of the current heuristic framework. Parameter tuning within this architecture appears to have reached diminishing returns. Key failures included temporal awareness features and cross-instance memory mechanisms, which introduced instability without improving packing efficiency. Successful techniques centered on local state analysis (entropy of remaining capacities) and carefully calibrated fixed bonuses that encourage space reuse without overcomplicating decision logic. For future research, recommendations include: (1) exploring alternative entropy formulations or complementary metrics like variance of remaining capacities, (2) testing different bonus structures such as residual space utilization ratios, (3) investigating machine learning approaches that can learn from packing outcomes without requiring explicit trend detection, and (4) considering hybrid strategies that combine online heuristics with limited look-ahead capabilities where feasible.

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Hybrid priority function combining CV-adaptive Best Fit with implicit trend detection.
    
    Implementation idea: Extend the successful CV-adaptive Best Fit heuristic (Parent #69) 
    with lightweight distribution estimation based on current bin state patterns to enable 
    implicit anticipation of future item trends. Instead of maintaining explicit state, 
    use capacity fragmentation patterns (skewness of remaining capacities, density of 
    small bins) to estimate likely future item characteristics and adjust gap thresholds 
    accordingly. This maintains online constraints while providing implicit foresight.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute state-based statistics for adaptive parameters
    n_bins = len(bins_remain_cap)
    if n_bins > 0:
        mean_remaining = np.mean(bins_remain_cap)
        std_remaining = np.std(bins_remain_cap)
        # Coefficient of variation as an adaptation signal (from parent solutions)
        cv = std_remaining / mean_remaining if mean_remaining > 0 else 0
        
        # Calculate skewness as a measure of capacity distribution asymmetry
        if std_remaining > 0:
            skewness = np.mean(((bins_remain_cap - mean_remaining) / std_remaining) ** 3)
        else:
            skewness = 0
            
        # Density of small bins (bins with capacity < 30% of initial capacity)
        small_bin_density = np.sum(bins_remain_cap < 30.0) / n_bins if n_bins > 0 else 0
        
        # Adaptive parameters based on state statistics
        # Use skewness to detect potential bimodal patterns in remaining capacities
        skew_factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * abs(skewness)  # Amplify when there's asymmetry
        
        # Base gap threshold from successful parent solution
        base_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.42, 9.0)
        
        # Adjust gap threshold based on both CV and skewness
        cv_adjustment = 1.0 + 0.1 * cv
        adaptive_gap_threshold = base_gap_threshold * cv_adjustment * skew_factor
        
        # Adjust penalty multiplier based on state statistics
        base_penalty_multiplier = 5.5
        penalty_multiplier = base_penalty_multiplier * cv_adjustment * skew_factor
        
        # Adaptive perfect fit bonus based on small bin density
        perfect_fit_bonus_base = item * 0.3
        # Increase bonus when there are many small bins (fragmentation risk)
        fragmentation_factor = 1.0 + 0.2 * small_bin_density
        perfect_fit_bonus = perfect_fit_bonus_base * fragmentation_factor
        
        # Utilization score based on state statistics
        bin_initial_capacity = 100.0
        utilization_after_placement = (bin_initial_capacity - remaining_after_placement) / bin_initial_capacity
        # Weight utilization score based on CV (more important when distribution is varied)
        utilization_weight = 0.2 * (1.0 + 0.1 * cv)
        utilization_score = np.where(
            remaining_after_placement >= 0,
            utilization_after_placement * utilization_weight,
            0.0
        )
        
    else:
        # Default values if no bins
        adaptive_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.42, 9.0)
        penalty_multiplier = 5.5
        perfect_fit_bonus = item * 0.3
        utilization_score = np.zeros_like(remaining_after_placement)
    
    # Gap-avoidance component: penalize bins that leave small gaps
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= 0) & (remaining_after_placement < adaptive_gap_threshold),
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Perfect fit bonus: reward bins that would be exactly filled
    perfect_fit_bonus_array = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement) < 1e-6,  # Account for floating point precision
        perfect_fit_bonus,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Matching bonus: reward bins that leave capacity suitable for items of similar size
    # This helps with bimodal distributions where similar items appear in clusters
    matching_target = item * 0.3  # Target for leaving room for another similar item
    matching_tolerance = item * 0.1  # Allow some variance
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - matching_target) < matching_tolerance,
        item * 0.15,  # Moderate bonus for good matches
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine components to compute final scores
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + perfect_fit_bonus_array + utilization_score + matching_bonus
    
    return scores

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Simplified CV-adaptive Best Fit heuristic based on successful parent solutions.
    
    Implementation follows the proven approach from parent solutions that showed
    simpler, more conservative adaptive heuristics outperform complex fragmentation-based approaches.
    
    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute state-based statistics for adaptive parameters
    n_bins = len(bins_remain_cap)
    if n_bins > 0:
        mean_remaining = np.mean(bins_remain_cap)
        std_remaining = np.std(bins_remain_cap)
        # Coefficient of variation as an adaptation signal (from parent solutions)
        cv = std_remaining / mean_remaining if mean_remaining > 0 else 0
        
        # Base gap threshold from successful parent solution
        base_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.42, 9.0)
        
        # Adjust gap threshold based on CV only (conservative approach from parents)
        cv_adjustment = 1.0 + 0.1 * cv
        adaptive_gap_threshold = base_gap_threshold * cv_adjustment
        
        # Adjust penalty multiplier based on CV only
        base_penalty_multiplier = 5.5
        penalty_multiplier = base_penalty_multiplier * cv_adjustment
        
        # Perfect fit bonus (from parent solutions)
        perfect_fit_bonus = item * 0.3
        
        # Utilization score with conservative weighting
        bin_initial_capacity = 100.0
        utilization_after_placement = (bin_initial_capacity - remaining_after_placement) / bin_initial_capacity
        # Weight utilization score based on CV (more important when distribution is varied)
        utilization_weight = 0.2
        utilization_score = utilization_after_placement * utilization_weight
        
    else:
        # Default values if no bins
        adaptive_gap_threshold = max(item * 0.42, 9.0)
        penalty_multiplier = 5.5
        perfect_fit_bonus = item * 0.3
        utilization_score = np.zeros_like(remaining_after_placement)
    
    # Gap-avoidance component: penalize bins that leave small gaps
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= 0) & (remaining_after_placement < adaptive_gap_threshold),
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Perfect fit bonus: reward bins that would be exactly filled
    perfect_fit_bonus_array = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement) < 1e-6,  # Account for floating point precision
        perfect_fit_bonus,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine components to compute final scores
    scores = best_fit_score - gap_penalty + perfect_fit_bonus_array + utilization_score
    
    return scores

The experiment series revealed that simplicity and conservative adaptation significantly outperform complex, multi-component heuristics in the online bin packing problem. Initially, an over-engineered solution incorporating skewness-based adjustments, small-bin density metrics, matching bonuses, and dynamic utilization weighting was tested (Experiment #1), yielding a suboptimal score of 2060.4 (3.21% excess). This degraded performance compared to known parent solutions demonstrated that added complexity introduced instability rather than foresight. In response, the heuristic was simplified to retain only core components proven effective in high-performing parent solutions: CV-adaptive Best Fit scoring, gap-avoidance penalties scaled by coefficient of variation (CV), a fixed perfect fit bonus (item × 0.3), and a lightweight utilization score with constant weight (0.2). This streamlined approach (Experiment #2) achieved a score of 2050.8 (2.72% excess), matching the best parent solution exactly and confirming that minimal, well-tuned adaptive mechanisms are more robust than attempts to implicitly model future item distributions through bin-state fragmentation patterns. Key parameter insights include: (1) the gap threshold formula max(item × 0.42, 9.0) and penalty multiplier 5.5 are highly effective and sensitive to change; (2) CV-based adaptation with a modest scaling factor (1.0 + 0.1 × CV) provides sufficient responsiveness without overfitting to transient bin states; (3) additional bonuses (e.g., for matching similar items) or dynamic weights based on bin statistics consistently degrade performance. Persistent challenges include the inability to effectively anticipate bimodal or clustered item size distributions without violating online constraints—approaches attempting to do so via capacity skewness or small-bin density failed. The most successful technique was disciplined simplification: removing all non-essential components and adhering closely to empirically validated parent designs. Unresolved issues center around fundamental limitations of purely reactive heuristics; true improvement may require lightweight learned models (e.g., fixed lookup tables trained offline on distribution features) that respect online constraints but encode broader statistical knowledge. Actionable recommendations for future research include: (1) exploring pre-trained, static regressors that map current item size and aggregate bin statistics (like CV) to optimal gap thresholds, trained on historical instance data; (2) testing alternative base heuristics beyond Best Fit, such as refined variants of First Fit Decreasing adapted for online use; (3) investigating whether a small, fixed set of expert heuristics can be selected dynamically using a meta-heuristic based on real-time CV and item size trends, without maintaining state. Overall, the experiments underscore that in online combinatorial optimization, robustness through simplicity often surpasses sophistication.

import numpy as np

def priority(item: float, bins_remain_cap: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Priority function with variance-based dynamic parameter adjustment.
    
    Implementation: Replace entropy-based fragmentation measurement with a variance-based
    metric that directly quantifies the dispersion of remaining bin capacities. Compute 
    the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean) of bins_remain_cap 
    to detect high-fragmentation states more robustly than entropy. Use this metric to 
    modulate gap penalties and bonus weights in a manner analogous to the current 
    entropy_factor. This approach better captures pathological fragmentation patterns 
    that entropy smooths over, potentially closing part of the persistent 32-bin 
    optimality gap.

    Args:
        item: Size of the current item to be placed (float)
        bins_remain_cap: NumPy array of remaining capacities of valid bins (those that can fit the item) (float array)

    Returns:
        NumPy array of priority scores for each valid bin
    """
    # Return empty array if no valid bins
    if len(bins_remain_cap) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    # Calculate remaining capacity after placing the current item
    remaining_after_placement = bins_remain_cap - item
    
    # Basic Best Fit component: prioritize bins with least remaining capacity after placement
    best_fit_score = -remaining_after_placement  # Higher score for smaller remaining capacity
    
    # Compute local statistics to inform dynamic parameter adjustment
    # Use coefficient of variation (std/mean) as a measure of fragmentation
    cap_mean = np.mean(bins_remain_cap)
    if cap_mean > 0 and len(bins_remain_cap) > 1:
        cap_std = np.std(bins_remain_cap)
        # Coefficient of variation - measures relative dispersion
        coef_variation = cap_std / cap_mean
        # Normalize by maximum possible coefficient of variation for the current state
        # In the worst case, std could be roughly equal to mean, so we normalize accordingly
        # We cap the effect to avoid extreme values
        normalized_variability = min(coef_variation, 2.0)
    else:
        normalized_variability = 0.0
    
    # Use variability to adjust parameters dynamically
    # Higher variability suggests more fragmented bins, so increase gap penalty
    variability_factor = 1.0 + 0.85 * normalized_variability
    
    # Set parameters based on variability factor (using proven values from parent solution)
    gap_threshold = max(item * 0.40, 6.0) * variability_factor
    penalty_multiplier = 7.0 * variability_factor
    
    # Apply penalty to bins with small remaining capacity after placement
    gap_penalty = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < gap_threshold,
        remaining_after_placement * penalty_multiplier,
        0.0
    )
    
    # Fixed percentage-based matching bonus (from parent solution)
    matching_target = item * 0.2
    matching_tolerance = item * 0.05  # Fixed tolerance based on item size
    matching_bonus = np.where(
        np.abs(remaining_after_placement - matching_target) < matching_tolerance,
        item * 0.22,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Efficiency bonus for bins that would be nearly filled (from parent solution)
    efficiency_threshold = max(item * 0.1, 2.0)  # Minimum absolute threshold
    efficiency_bonus = np.where(
        remaining_after_placement < efficiency_threshold,
        item * 0.18,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Consolidation bonus for bins that would leave moderate residual space (from parent solution)
    consolidation_lower = item * 0.1
    consolidation_upper = item * 0.3
    
    consolidation_bonus = np.where(
        (remaining_after_placement >= consolidation_lower) & 
        (remaining_after_placement <= consolidation_upper),
        item * 0.08,  # Proven value from parent solution
        0.0
    )
    
    # Combine all components
    scores = (best_fit_score - gap_penalty + 
              matching_bonus + efficiency_bonus + consolidation_bonus)
    
    return scores
